subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class one-line localhost plus Telegram owner bootstrap surface, and should the supported shape live in non-interactive onboarding, a dedicated bootstrap command, or plugin-owned setup hooks?
rationale: The request crosses gateway service lifecycle, dashboard auth token handling, Telegram credentials, and DM owner authorization, so automation needs maintainer intent before implementation can safely choose the public API and trust boundary.

options.title: Design First-Class Bootstrap
options.body: Define a supported setup surface that preserves numeric allowlist or verified owner-preapproval semantics, then implement it across onboarding, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow To Telegram Owner Setup
options.body: Keep this umbrella as context while narrower Telegram owner/allowlist issues carry the first implementation step.

options.title: Defer Wrapper Surface
options.body: Keep setup terminal-first for now and document secure manual composition instead of adding a convenience wrapper.

recommendation.title: Design First-Class Bootstrap
recommendation.body: Define a supported setup surface that preserves numeric allowlist or verified owner-preapproval semantics, then implement it across onboarding, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal spans onboarding, dashboard auth, Telegram setup, and setup/product boundary work.
